newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends mixed as TWI rises, offshore weakens.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends mixed as TWI rises, offshore weakens.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ short end holds gains, reluctant to rally on TWI
* Bonds sell on global weakness, flirt with 8.00 pct support
New Zealand bank bills managed to hold onto their early gains by Thursday's close but the bond curve came under selling pressure in the face of foreign market weakness.
The 90-day bank bills closed on their open of 7.60 percent, despite a move higher in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index to 68.20 from its 67.90 open.

Dealers said the TWI strength did not seem to be feeding through into short rates. While there was a hesitancy to follow-through on a stronger currency given its recent volatility, the market seemed quick to sell on any indication of renewed weakness.
The June futures contract ended two basis points stronger at 92.26, with 2,430 contracts traded.

Bond dealers said flows had been reasonably quiet and mainly offshore-driven. U.S. Treasuries remained weighed down by the prospect of a monetary policy tightening at the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting on Tuesday, and Australian bonds had performed particularly poorly on the day.

"That has turned up the noses of the potential buyers, I guess. A general lack of confidence is filtering through the market at the moment, although later on this afternoon we have seen a little bit of buying interest coming through from domestic clients," one dealer said.
"There's very little out in the way of announcements in the States, which might be encouraging people to take advantage of the higher rates today," she said.

The 11/06 maturity traded as high as 7.90 percent during the session but finished at 7.88 percent. Dealers said global sentiment was bearish and fear was growing that the longer New Zealand bonds would not be able to hold beneath 8.00 percent, a break of which would cause a significant jump higher.
